definition.value: A quantification unit used to express the dimensionless ratio between two quantitative measurements.

Peptide-to-protein aggregation using Tukey's median polish algorithm.
Row and column medians are iteratively removed from the peptide
intensity matrix until convergence, producing protein-level summaries
that are robust to outlier peptides and systematic row or column
effects. Default aggregation method in MSstats.
A molecular entity or mass spectrometry-derived feature for which a quantitative abundance measurement is determined in a proteomics experiment.
A normalization method in which measurements are iteratively adjusted using pairwise LOESS smoothing to remove systematic intensity-dependent biases across samples.

comment.value: The method iteratively removes pairwise intensity-dependent biases across samples. It is computationally intensive and assumes the majority of features are not differentially abundant.

definition.value: A software that has the function of generating graphical or visual representations of data for interpretation or communication.
A peptide-spectrum match associated with a quantitative measurement derived from the corresponding mass spectrum or its associated ion signals.
A label-based quantification approach in which chemical reagents are used to covalently modify peptides or proteins for quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.
The ratio of the mean or other summary abundance in one experimental condition to that in a reference condition.

comment.value: Fold change conventionally represents relative abundance between treatment and control. Directionality should be explicitly specified because FC > 1 and FC < 1 are asymmetric representations of up- and down-regulation.

definition.value: A value or a set of values obtained by applying a Method to data
A data transformation method in which measurements are transformed using the logarithm with base 10.

comment.value: The method reduces right-skewness. The method is undefined for zero or negative values without offset.

definition.value: A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are estimated using a low-rank approximation of the data matrix derived from singular value decomposition.

comment.value: SVD imputation assumes linear structure and may bias results when missingness is extensive or non-random.

definition.value: A data transformation method in which measurements are transformed using the natural logarithm with base e.

comment.value: The method reduces right-skewness. The method is undefined for zero or negative values without offset.

definition.value: An isobaric labeling batch in which samples are labeled with distinct Tandem Mass Tag (TMT) reagent channels and combined for multiplexed quantitative mass spectrometry analysis.

A spectral count-based quantification method that calculates the Normalized Spectral Abundance Factor (NSAF) by dividing each protein's spectral count by its sequence length and normalizing the resulting value across all quantified proteins.

Aggregation using only the N most intense input features per target
feature. Features are ranked by intensity and only the top N are
included in the reduction step. The reduction operator (mean, median,
or sum) applied to the selected features must be specified. N is a
required parameter.
A post-translational or chemical modification for which a quantitative abundance or relative occupancy measurement is determined from mass spectrometry data.
A processing method that projects values onto a smaller number of derived variables while preserving a stated property of the data
Scaling adjusts the magnitude or variance of features and modifies the spread (range or variance) of values typically across samples.

comment.value: Scaling changes the relative influence of features. Scaling prevents high-variant features from dominating multivariate analyses.

definition.value: An effect size measuring the strength and direction of associations between two quantitative variables.
A quantification unit used to express the amount of an analyte per specified volume, mass, or other reference quantity.
A dimensionality reduction method that projects high-dimensional data into a lower-dimensional space using linear combinations of the original features.
An intensity-based quantification method that estimates peptide or protein abundance from precursor ion signal intensities measured in MS1 spectra, typically using extracted ion chromatograms.
A statistical measure used to quantify evidence against a null hypothesis, the significance of an observed result, or the estimated reliability of a statistical finding.
The base-10 logarithm of the fold change between two experimental conditions.

comment.value: log10 fold change is less common than log2 fold change in proteomics. A value of 1 corresponds to a 10-fold increase and −1 to a 10-fold decrease.

definition.value: A normalization method in which measurements are transformed so that all samples share an identical empirical intensity distribution.
A stable isotope labeling method that chemically modifies peptide amino groups through reductive dimethylation using isotopically distinct reagents for relative quantification.
A data transformation method in which measurements are transformed using the square root.

comment.value: The method moderately stabilizes variance.
The method reduces right-skewness. The method is undefined for negative values without offset.

definition.value: A peptide with a defined molecular composition, including its modifications and their localization where known, for which a quantitative abundance measurement is determined.
An input constraint that retains only peptide or modification-site measurements for which the relevant modification or molecular feature has been confidently localized.
An effect size expressing the strength or magnitude of the relationship between two or more variables generated from contingency tables.
A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced with a value of zero.

comment.value: Zero imputation implicitly assumes absence of signal and can strongly distort distributions and fold-change estimates, particularly when missing values arise from limits of detection rather than true absence.

definition.value: The difference between the means of two groups divided by a pooled within-group standard deviation.

comment.value: Cohen's D Commonly used for proteomics differential-abundance comparisons. For independent groups, the pooled SD is typically calculated from both groups; variants exist for paired designs.

definition.value: A normalization method in which measurements are normalized based on the upper quartile of the intensity distribution for each sample.
A spectral count-based quantification method that estimates protein abundance using the number of accepted peptide-spectrum matches assigned to a protein or protein group.
An input constraint that permits the use of unique peptides and shared peptides assigned to a single protein or protein group according to a protein inference rule.
A batch correction method in which principal components associated with batch-related variation are identified and removed or regressed out from data.

comment.value: The method removes variance associated with batch-linked principal components. The method has the risk of overcorrection if components capture biological signal.

definition.value: A weighting scheme that assigns weights to quantitative measurements based on their signal intensities, giving greater influence to measurements with higher intensities.

Peptide-to-protein aggregation using the MaxLFQ algorithm. Protein
intensities are calculated from the most consistently quantified
peptides across samples using an intensity ratio-based approach that
maximizes the number of quantification pairs. Implemented in MaxQuant
and available in other tools including DIA-NN and FragPipe/IonQuant.
An abundance unit expressing the estimated number of molecules or molecular copies of an analyte in a specified sample or biological system.
Ratio of the odds of an outcome between two groups.

comment.value: Odds ratio is derived from contingency table of categorical variables.

definition.value: A normalization method in which measurements are normalized by values derived from sample-specific intensity quantiles.

comment.value: Typically the method is based on the 75th percentile (upper quartile) of the distribution of sample measurements.

definition.value: A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by a random value drawn from a normal distribution that is truncated to a specified range, typically constrained to low-intensity values to model left-censored measurements near the limit of detection.

comment.value: Truncated normal distribution imputation assumes missing values arise from censoring rather than true absence and is sensitive to the choice of truncation bounds, mean shift, and variance parameters, introducing controlled stochasticity into the data.

definition.value: A quantitative measure describing the magnitude of a difference or association, independently of statistical significance and, where applicable, sample size.
A label-free quantification method that estimates peptide or protein abundance using measured mass spectrometric signal intensities.
A quantification approach that determines differences or ratios in peptide or protein abundance between samples, conditions, or reference measurements.
A normalization method in which measurements are normalized so that the mean intensity is equal across samples.
A scaling method in which measurements are standardized using robust estimates of central tendency and dispersion, such as the median and median absolute deviation.

comment.value: Standardization produces mean of 0 and variance of 1.

definition.value: A label or identifier assigned to a specific quantification channel in a multiplexed proteomics experiment, distinguishing it from other channels within the same labeling scheme.
An input constraint that retains only quantitative entities observed in at least a specified number (K) of samples, channels, or experimental conditions.

An isobaric labeling channel within a Tandem Mass Tag (TMT) labeling scheme, associated with a specific TMT reagent that generates a distinguishable reporter ion for relative quantification in multiplexed mass spectrometry.
A scaling method in which measurements are scaled using the median absolute deviation to achieve robust dispersion.
Normalization removes systematic technical bias between samples and adjusts measurements within samples to make them comparable.

comment.value: Normalization addresses systematic technical variation between samples. This are effects such as differences in total ion current, sample loading differences, instrument drift, and batch effects.

definition.value: An input constraint that permits all available quantitative measurements to be used in a computational analysis without applying additional input-selection restrictions.
A batch correction method in which unwanted variation is estimated using control features, replicate samples, or residual structure and removed through factor analysis or regression modeling.

comment.value: The method requires appropriate control features or replicates. Misspecification can lead to under- or overcorrection.

definition.value: The difference between the means of two groups divided by the standard deviation of a designated reference/control group.

comment.value: Glass's delta is particularly useful when the experimental intervention may alter variability, making a pooled SD inappropriate.

definition.value: A computational strategy that assigns numerical weights to individual quantitative measurements to determine their relative contributions to an aggregated abundance estimate in a proteomics analysis.
A normalization method in which measurements are normalized relative to a designated reference, such as a pooled or common reference sample.

comment.value: The method reduces inter-batch variability using a shared reference. Its effectiveness depends on reference sample quality and consistency.

definition.value: An individual entry in a correction factor matrix that specifies the contribution of isotopic impurities from one isobaric labeling channel to another, used to correct reporter ion intensities in quantitative proteomics.

Label-free quantification aggregation using the original Cox et al.
2008 ratio-based approach, prior to the introduction of MaxLFQ.
Protein intensities are derived from the median of all pairwise
peptide intensity ratios across samples.
A supervised dimensionality reduction method that uses partial least squares (PLS) to derive latent components that maximize covariance between predictor variables and response variables.
A supervised linear dimensionality reduction method that uses linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to identify projections maximizing between-class separation relative to within-class variation.
A group of proteins that cannot be unambiguously distinguished based on the available peptide evidence and for which a collective quantitative abundance measurement is determined.
A linear dimensionality reduction method that approximates a data matrix using a specified number of its largest singular values and corresponding singular vectors.

comment.value: An effect size expressing the difference between two group means in original measurement units.

definition.value: A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that preserves local neighborhood relationships by reconstructing each observation from its neighbors and embedding the data in a lower-dimensional space.

A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by a random value drawn from a left-shifted probability distribution representing low-abundance signals near the limit of detection, with parameters chosen to assign minimal probability to higher intensities.

comment.value: minProb imputation models missing values as left-censored due to limited detectability. Results depend on distribution parameters (e.g., width and downshift) and introduce stochastic variability.

definition.value: A label-based quantification method that uses isobaric chemical tags to label multiple samples, enabling relative quantification through reporter ions generated during tandem mass spectrometry.
A computational procedure applied to proteomics data to transform, correct, normalize, or otherwise process quantitative measurements for subsequent analysis.
The estimated posterior probability that a reported identification or assignment is incorrect, conditional on the observed evidence and the statistical model.
A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are estimated iteratively using the expectation–maximization algorithm under an assumed statistical model of the data.

comment.value: EM imputation depends on distributional assumptions and may converge to local optima.

definition.value: A data transformation method in which measurements are transformed using the logarithm with base 2.

comment.value: The method reduces right-skewness. The method is undefined for zero or negative values without offset.

definition.value: A standardized statistical measure that expresses the deviation of an observed value from the mean of a reference distribution in units of its standard deviation.
A multiple-testing significance measure representing the minimum estimated false discovery rate at which a particular hypothesis would be considered significant.
A software that has the function of performing statistical analysis, including estimation, hypothesis testing, or modeling on data.
An abundance unit representing parts per million, corresponding to one part of an analyte per million parts of the reference quantity.
A processing method that assigns values to entries for which no measurement was obtained.
A multivariate statistical method that identifies pairs of linear combinations of variables from two datasets that maximize their mutual correlation.
A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are estimated using multivariate imputation by chained equations, iteratively modeling each feature conditional on all others.

comment.value: MICE supports flexible models but is computationally intensive and sensitive to model specification.

definition.value: A specification of an isobaric labeling scheme that defines the set of available labeling channels and their associated reporter ion masses for multiplexed quantitative mass spectrometry.

A matrix of correction factors describing the contributions of isotopic impurities between reporter ion channels in an isobaric labeling experiment, used to correct measured reporter ion intensities for isotopic interference.
A spectral count-based quantification method that calculates the Spectral Abundance Factor (SAF) by normalizing the spectral count assigned to a protein by its sequence length.
A procedure applied to proteomic data in order to produce, transform or summarise quantitative values

A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are estimated using Bayesian principal component analysis, modeling the data with a low-dimensional latent structure and incorporating uncertainty in the estimates.

comment.value: BPCA imputation captures global correlation structure but assumes approximate low-rank data and can oversmooth local variation.

definition.value: A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by a minimal deterministic value, typically set at the lowest observed intensity or just below the detection limit, to represent signals that are present but below the limit of detection.

comment.value: MinDet imputation is deterministic, preserves low-intensity signals, and is less stochastic than methods like MinProb imputation, but it can artificially reduce variance and bias downstream statistical analyses.

definition.value: A unit or measurement scale used to express a quantitative result in a proteomics analysis.
Precursor-level quantification
A weighting scheme that assigns identical weights to all included quantitative measurements, allowing each measurement to contribute equally to the aggregated estimate.
A software that has the function of transforming, normalizing, batch correcting, scaling, filtering, aligning, or otherwise modifying raw or intermediate measurement data.
A spectral count-based quantification method that estimates protein abundance from the number of assigned MS2 spectra or associated peptide-spectrum matches.
A protein for which a quantitative abundance measurement is determined from associated peptide measurements or other protein-specific mass spectrometry signals.
A normalization method in which measurements are normalized so that the total signal intensity (sum, mean, or median) is equal across samples.
A software that has the function of assigning biological, chemical, or molecular identities to measurement features or signals.
Difference between the median abundance values of two conditions.

comment.value: Useful when abundance is reported on a directly interpretable scale. Unlike standardized mean differences, it retains the original measurement units.

definition.value: An analytical or computational method used to estimate the abundance of peptides, proteins, or other molecular entities from mass spectrometry measurements.
A normalization method in which  measurements are normalized so that the median intensity is equal across samples.
A normalization method in which measurements are normalized relative to a designated internal reference, such as an internal standard.

comment.value: The method reduces inter-batch variability using a shared reference. Its effectiveness depends on reference sample quality and consistency.

definition.value: An input constraint that retains only the N highest-ranked quantitative entities according to a specified ranking criterion.

A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by the median of the observed values for the same feature (e.g., protein, peptide, or ion) across a defined set of samples or conditions.

comment.value: Median imputation is more robust to outliers than mean imputation but still reduces variance and may bias downstream analyses, especially when missingness is not random.

definition.value: A quantification approach that uses stable isotope labels or other distinguishable labeling reagents to measure peptide or protein abundance across samples.

A normalization method that combines the estimation of a mean-variance model with application of a variance-stabilizing trnasformation and between-sample normalization in order to produce variance-stabilized and normalized quantitative measurements.

comment.value: Variance stabilizing normalization (VSN) refers to model-based procedures that estimate parameters of an intensity-dependent variance function and apply a derived transformation while simultaneously performing normalization across samples. It is broader in scope than variance stabilizing transformation alone.

definition.value: A weighting scheme that assigns weights to quantitative measurements based on their estimated variances, typically giving greater influence to measurements with lower variance.

A batch correction method in which additive and multiplicative batch effects in data are modeled and adjusted using an empirical Bayes framework that shrinks batch-specific parameter estimates toward a pooled prior distribution.

comment.value: The method adjusts both location and scale effects. It requires correct batch annotation and assumes batch effects are separable from biological covariates included in the model.

definition.value: A quantification approach that selectively measures predefined peptides or proteins using mass spectrometry acquisition methods configured to monitor specific analytes.
An isobaric label-based quantification method that uses Tandem Mass Tag reagents to multiplex samples and determine relative peptide or protein abundances from mass spectrometry measurements.
A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that constructs a lower-dimensional representation from eigenvectors of a graph Laplacian derived from similarities between observations.
The base-2 logarithm of the fold change between two experimental conditions.

comment.value: log2 fold change is commonly used in proteomics because equal-magnitude increases and decreases are represented symmetrically: e.g. log2FC = 1 corresponds to a 2-fold increase and log2FC = −1 corresponds to a 2-fold decrease.

definition.value: A quantification unit used to express the amount or relative abundance of a molecular entity.

A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that uses t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) to represent high-dimensional observations in a low-dimensional space by minimizing divergence between neighborhood probability distributions.
A weighting scheme that assigns weights to quantitative measurements based on their associated identification or quality scores, according to a specified score-to-weight mapping.

Aggregation by arithmetic mean of input feature intensities for each
target feature. Missing values are excluded from the mean calculation
unless imputation has been applied prior to aggregation.
An adjusted p-value obtained using the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate across multiple hypothesis tests.

has_exact_synonym.value: quantile regression imputation of left-censored data

definition.value: A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are replaced by random values drawn from a left-censored distribution estimated by quantile regression on observed intensities, thereby modeling missingness as arising from signals below the limit of detection.

comment.value: QRILC imputation explicitly models left-censoring and preserves distributional structure of low-intensity values, but relies on assumptions about censoring behavior and the fitted regression model.

definition.value: A batch correction method that removes estimated batch-associated effects from a data matrix by fitting a linear model and subtracting the batch component, producing a batch-adjusted matrix.

comment.value: The method is applied post hoc to generate corrected data for visualization or unsupervised analysis. It requires correct batch annotation and assumes batch effects are separable from biological covariates included in the model.

definition.value: A metabolic labeling method that uses Stable Isotope Labeling by Amino Acids in Cell Culture (SILAC) to incorporate isotopically distinct amino acids into proteins for mass spectrometry-based quantification.
An input constraint that retains only identifications or quantitative measurements satisfying a specified confidence threshold.

A collection of Tandem Mass Tag (TMT) isobaric labeling reagents designed for multiplexed quantitative mass spectrometry, comprising chemically isobaric tags with distinct reporter ion masses that enable relative quantification of multiple samples within a single analysis.
A range of values, computed from the data at a stated confidence level, that is expected to contain the true value of a population parameter such as a mean difference or fold change.

A batch correction method that extends the ComBat empirical Bayes framework to count-based data using generalized linear models with appropriate distributional assumptions (negative binomial distribution).

comment.value: The method is designed primarily for sequencing count data. It is less commonly applied to continuous intensity-based mass spectrometry data. It requires correct batch annotation and assumes batch effects are separable from biological covariates included in the model.

definition.value: A method for reducing ratio compression
A test statistic expressing an estimated difference or coefficient relative to its standard error and evaluated against a Student's t-distribution under the null hypothesis.
Kendall rank correlation coefficient measuring the ordinal association between two variables.

common.value: Kendall rank correlation is less common than Pearson or Spearman correlation, but is useful for ranked or ordinal associations.

definition.value: A normalization method in which measurements are adjusted using locally weighted regression to correct intensity-dependent systematic biases.
Ratio of hazard rates between two groups over time.

comment.value: Hazard ratio is relevant for survival/time-to-event analyses using continous variables as a predictor.

definition.value: A group of samples labeled with distinct isobaric reagent channels and combined for analysis within a single multiplexed quantitative mass spectrometry experiment.
A bias-corrected standardized mean difference obtained by applying a small-sample correction to a standardized mean difference, commonly Cohen’s d.

comment.value: Hedge's g is often preferred to Cohen’s d for small sample sizes because the correction reduces small-sample bias.

definition.value: A chemical labeling approach that introduces stable isotopes into peptides or proteins to generate distinguishable mass signatures for quantitative comparison.
An adjusted p-value obtained using the Bonferroni procedure to control the family-wise error rate by accounting for the number of statistical hypotheses tested.
Difference between the mean abundance values of two conditions.

comment.value: Useful when abundance is reported on a directly interpretable scale. Unlike standardized mean differences, it retains the original measurement units.

definition.value: A software that has the function of determining numerical abundance or concentration values from experimental measurement data.

A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by a random value drawn from a normal distribution whose mean is shifted to lower values relative to the observed data distribution, typically with reduced variance, to represent low-abundance signals near the limit of detection.

comment.value: Downshifted normal distribution imputation assumes missing values are left-censored and introduces stochastic low-intensity values; outcomes are sensitive to the chosen mean shift and variance parameters.

definition.value:
Aggregation by median of input feature intensities for each target
feature. Missing values are excluded from the median calculation unless
imputation has been applied prior to aggregation. More robust to
outlier peptides than mean aggregation.
A weighting scheme that assigns weights to quantitative measurements based on the properties or quality of their associated precursor–fragment ion transitions.

A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is estimated from a weighted or unweighted aggregate (e.g., mean or median) of the corresponding measurements in the k most similar features or samples, where similarity is defined by a distance metric computed on observed data.

comment.value: k-nearest neighbors imputation leverages local similarity structure in the data but is sensitive to the choice of k, distance metric, and data scaling, and may perform poorly when missingness is extensive.

definition.value: A label-based quantification approach that incorporates isotopically labeled metabolic precursors into proteins during biological synthesis, enabling quantitative comparison by mass spectrometry.
A result obtained from a statistical analysis of quantitative data, including measures of variability, uncertainty, association, effect size, or statistical significance.

A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that uses Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) to construct a low-dimensional embedding by optimizing a representation of the data's neighborhood relationships.
A missing value imputation method in which missing measurements are predicted using an ensemble of decision trees trained iteratively on observed values.

comment.value: MissForest captures nonlinear relationships but may introduce bias and has high computational cost for large datasets.

definition.value: A peptide sequence for which a quantitative abundance measurement is determined by aggregating or evaluating associated mass spectrometry signals.
A program or suite of programs that implements one or more Methods
A multiple-testing-adjusted significance measure obtained using a procedure designed to control or estimate the false discovery rate among rejected hypotheses.

A computational method used to combine multiple quantitative measurements into a single representative value at a specified level of aggregation, such as peptide, protein, or protein group, in a quantitative proteomics analysis.
A test statistic formed as a ratio of variance-related estimates and evaluated against an F-distribution under the null hypothesis.
Spearman rank correlation coefficient measures the strength and direction of a monotonic association between two variables.

comment.value: Spearman rank correlation is useful when variable distributions are non-normal or relationships are monotonic but not necessarily linear.

definition.value: A quantitative measurement or derived estimate representing the abundance, concentration, relative amount, or change in abundance of a molecular entity in a proteomics experiment.

An individual quantification channel within an isobaric labeling scheme, associated with a specific labeling reagent that produces a distinguishable reporter ion for relative quantification of samples in multiplexed mass spectrometry.
A processing method that brings measurements from separate acquisitions onto a common retention time or feature axis.
A scaling method in which measurements are centered and scaled to have zero mean and unit variance.
A TMT-based quantification method that uses reporter ion intensities measured in MS2 fragmentation spectra to estimate relative peptide or protein abundance across labeling channels.

A collection of isobaric labeling reagents designed for multiplexed quantitative mass spectrometry, comprising chemically equivalent tags with distinct reporter ion masses that enable relative quantification of multiple samples within a single analysis.
A specification of the experimental setup, including sample organization, labeling strategies, and other design parameters used in a quantitative proteomics experiment.
A test statistic calculated from squared deviations or related quantities and evaluated against a chi-square distribution under the null hypothesis.
A dimensionless measure of relative variability calculated as the standard deviation divided by the mean of a set of measurements.
A dimensionality reduction method that uses nonlinear transformations to represent high-dimensional data in a lower-dimensional space while preserving selected structural relationships.

An isobaric label-based quantification method that uses Isobaric Tags for Relative and Absolute Quantitation (iTRAQ) reagents to determine peptide or protein abundance from reporter ion intensities in tandem mass spectrometry.
An input constraint that retains only peptides uniquely attributable to a single protein or protein group for quantitative analysis.
Pearson correlation coefficient measuring the strength and direction of a linear association between two quantitative variables.
Transformation has the purpose of changing the distributional shape and variance of the structure of the data

comment.value: Transformation changes within-sample distributional properties, not cross-sample comparability.

definition.value: A quantification approach that estimates the absolute amount or concentration of an analyte, typically using calibrated reference standards or another validated quantitative model.

A computational method used to identify, estimate, or reduce systematic technical variation between experimental batches while aiming to preserve biologically relevant variation in quantitative proteomics data.
A specification of the requirements or restrictions that input data must satisfy to be considered valid for a particular computational method or processing step in a quantitative proteomics workflow.
A p-value modified using a multiple-testing correction procedure to account for the simultaneous evaluation of multiple statistical hypotheses.
A linear dimensionality reduction method that uses principal component analysis (PCA) to project data onto orthogonal directions of maximum variance.
An effect size expressing the difference between two group means in units of a standard deviation.

comment.value: Appropriate when abundance measurements from two groups are compared on a standardized scale. Cohen’s d, Glass’s Δ, and Hedges’ g are standardized mean-difference measures.

definition.value: A normalization method in which measurements are normalized relative to a designated reference channel, commonly used in isobaric labeling experiments.
An input constraint that retains only quantitative entities with valid observations across all required samples, channels, or experimental conditions.
A quantification approach that estimates peptide or protein abundance directly from mass spectrometry measurements without introducing isotope or chemical labeling reagents.
An abundance unit representing parts per billion, corresponding to one part of an analyte per billion parts of the reference quantity.
A data transformation method in which measurements are transformed to reduce or eliminate dependence of the variance of the mean, thereby approdimating heteroscedasticity across the intensity range.

comment.value: Variance stabilizing transformation (VST) is typically applied to high-throughput quantitative data exhibiting mean–variance dependence. The transformation may be parametric or non-parametric and does not necessarily include between-sample scaling or normalization.

definition.value: An aggregation method in which multiple quantitative measurements are combined internally by a proteomics analysis software engine using its built-in aggregation procedure, without requiring a separately specified aggregation algorithm.
A targeted quantification method that uses Parallel Reaction Monitoring (PRM) to acquire high-resolution fragment ion spectra of selected precursor ions for peptide quantification.
A numerical quantity calculated from sample data and used to evaluate a statistical hypothesis according to a specified sampling distribution or testing procedure.
A quantification unit or measurement scale used to express the magnitude of a mass spectrometric signal associated with an analyte.
An input constraint that retains only the highest-scoring identification or measurement among competing candidates according to a specified scoring criterion.

A targeted quantification method that uses Selected or Multiple Reaction Monitoring (SRM/MRM) to measure predefined precursor-to-fragment ion transitions for quantitative analysis of specific peptides.
A fragment ion generated from a peptide precursor for which a quantitative signal intensity or abundance measurement is determined by mass spectrometry.

Intensity-based absolute quantification. The sum of peptide intensities
for a protein is divided by the number of theoretically observable
tryptic peptides (peptides between 6 and 30 amino acids). Provides an
approximation of molar abundance enabling comparison across proteins
within a sample.
A scaling method in which measurements are linearly rescaled to a fixed range, typically between zero and one.

A missing value imputation method in which each missing measurement is replaced by the arithmetic mean of the observed values for the same feature (e.g., protein, peptide, or ion) across a defined set of samples or conditions.

comment.value: Mean imputation preserves the feature mean but reduces variance and can bias downstream statistical analyses, particularly in the presence of non-random missingness.

definition.value: A label-free quantification approach that estimates protein abundance from the number of tandem mass spectra or peptide-spectrum matches assigned to a protein.
An aggregation method explicitly selected and applied by the user to combine multiple quantitative measurements into a representative value at a specified level of a proteomics analysis.
A normalization method in whichmeasurements are normalized by the maximum absolute value observed for each feature or sample.
A dimensionality reduction method that uses known class labels, response variables, or other supervised information to construct a lower-dimensional representation of the data.
An input constraint that permits peptides mapping to multiple proteins or protein groups to contribute to quantitative analysis.
An input constraint that retains only monitored precursor–fragment ion transitions considered specific to the target analyte for quantitative analysis.
A scaling method in which measurements are scaled so that each sample vector has unit length.
A batch correction method in which batch effects are modeled as covariates in a linear modeling framework and adjusted during model fitting.

comment.value: Batch variables are included as covariates in a linear modeling framework during differential abundance analysis, allowing batch effects to be adjusted during parameter estimation rather than by directly modifying the data matrix. The method is suitable for complex experimental designs. This approach preserves raw values but adjusts estimated contrasts. Appropriate when the primary goal is hypothesis testing rather than data visualization. It requires correct batch annotation and assumes batch effects are separable from biological covariates included in the model.

definition.value: An effect size expressing the relative magnitude of a quantitative measurement between two groups or conditions as a ratio.

comment.value: Ratio effect sizes include fold change and logarithmically transformed fold changes.

definition.value: A weighting scheme that assigns weights to quantitative measurements based on their associated confidence estimates, giving greater influence to measurements considered more reliable.

Aggregation by summation of all input feature intensities for each
target feature. All qualifying input features contribute equally with
no weighting. Missing values are excluded from the sum unless a
zero-fill imputation has been applied prior to aggregation.
The probability, under a specified null hypothesis and statistical model, of obtaining a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed value.

A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that estimates geodesic distances between observations on a neighborhood graph and uses multidimensional scaling to construct a lower-dimensional embedding.
